gaps.text: Still the 36-line stub: 8 grey boxes, tan plane, NO ceiling at all. Biggest gap in the project.

Content gap, not a rendering gap. (1) Product facings are flat colour fields with grey bars instead of real printed type — ~60% of the tell. (2) ~8 box meshes recoloured, 5-8 identical copies per shelf; real shelves carry 6-15 SKUs of mixed height/width and something on nearly every shelf is a bottle/jar/pouch/bag. (3) Zero 'shopped' disorder — every face perfectly flush, unrotated, evenly spaced, no sold-out voids.

Contact shadows / AO is now the single biggest tell — products have no darkening where they meet the deck, shelf cavities do not fall off to near-black, so shelves read as decals floating on a plane. Then: no per-instance variation WITHIN a facing block (20 identical chip bags, same lean, zero gaps); shelves 100% full when real stores run 10-20% gaps; everything the same matte diffuse with zero specular events.

The two surfaces filling the largest solid angle of the frame — ceiling and floor — are still flat-shaded planes with a texture on them. (1) The floor returns ZERO specular under a lit ceiling; every real photo shows the ceiling light rows mirrored as long vertical smears. 'Until light physically bounces off the floor, nothing further up the list will matter.' (2) Ceiling troffers are emissive quads coplanar with the tile, not recessed housings with tube shapes and a shadow line. (3) BINARY TELLS: an unlit pink placeholder cube on a grey stick, untextured grey cart proxies, a blank grey plane where a sign texture failed. Any one ends the test alone.

bench() measures a starting geometry the game never produces. bench() spawns the cop 4.32m BEHIND the thief (gapMul 0.96 x suspicionRadius, already at 0.7x copRun). game.js enterFloor(i) spawns him at (aisleX(i), 0, -AISLE_LEN/2+3) — the MOUTH of the thief's aisle, between the thief and the only exit. Measured from the real start with powerups deleted from the store: 100% catch, no powerup (80/80 controlled, 14/14 full end-to-end game loop), chase over in ~1.2s median. Root cause is geometry, not speed: a corked 4m aisle is impassable — the thief's own nav avoid radius (1.8m, agents.js navToExit bolt case) is WIDER than the aisle half-lane (AISLE_GAP/2 - BODY_R = 1.58m), so he can never route around a cop standing in it and walks straight into the 1.15m catchRadius. Give him a way through (second exit / back-of-store route / a juke or shove past a blocking body), THEN re-run bench() from enterFloor()'s spawn — that is the only number that describes the game.

Catch median from dispatch is 1.13s - FASTER than round 2's 1.7s. The 68->73% headline came from adding an escape hatch (25% route out the back, 0/270 caught if you follow), not from making the catches harder.

cop.note: ROOT CAUSE: the neck sat at hips-local 0.60 while the torso capsule's top cap was at 0.71, with a head sphere of radius 0.135 - so 96% of every head in the game was INSIDE its own torso. What poked out was a 25mm skullcap, the hair hemisphere covered that, and on the cop the cap covered the hair. 'He's just kinda black, he doesn't have a face' was literally true: there was no head above the shoulders to put a face on. Feet also ended 85mm above the floor, so everyone was hovering. Three more bugs: every taper() in the file was inverted (thighs flaring at the knee, forearms fattest at the wrist), an atlas material without a UV cell gave him a white apron reading CHOP across his stomach, and flat plates on a curved chest needed pitch and yaw not just z.

audio.note: It DISPROVED my hypothesis before trusting it: muting the whole pa bus left the hiss intact and the speech bus reads exact digital silence when closed, so the round-3 open-channel hiss was properly gated all along. PA had two causes in audio: echoCancellation on speakers (Chrome's AEC references the page's own render stream, which contains the player's voice returning from the ceiling 10-200ms later - it was subtracting the thing it was protecting), and the voice arriving at parity with the bed so opening the channel made the mix 4.3 dBA QUIETER because the two ducks outweighed the voice they made room for. THIRD BUG found while validating: the howl watchdog had never fired and COULD not - it read the output of a 6:1 compressor thresholded at -26dBFS against 0.30 linear, which needs +85dBFS at its input. Rebuilt on the raw mic with a steadiness discriminator, because level alone cannot separate a shout from a howl.
audio.verdict: PASS on both bugs. HISS: airTop in bed.js used filt('highshelf', 5200, 0.7, 6) on pink noise - pink falls 3dB/octave, so a +6dB shelf spanning two octaves flattens it EXACTLY, generating WHITE noise above 5kHz, which is the definition of tape hiss. 11.2kHz band went -46.6 -> -69.8dB while everything below 5.6kHz moved under 2dB.

camera.note: THE FINDING: the old rig sat at 6.4m, ABOVE the 5.2m ceiling — the camera was outside the room, which is why the store read as a floor plan instead of a place. Now 2.36m: 31cm over the gondola decks, 11cm under the signage, so gondolas become walls and signs pass overhead. Yaw snaps to the store's grid bearings rather than the cop's heading, deliberately: main.js rotates input by yaw, so a camera chasing the heading closes a loop (hold D, heading turns, camera turns, D means somewhere else, cop pirouettes). IT OVERTURNED ITS OWN DESIGN: a planned gap-driven height rise measured +6 points of thief visibility against shelves modelled as 2.05m boxes from SHELF_H, but a raycast against the real scene found the blocker at 3.8m — an uncollidered sign gantry. There is nothing to see over. Re-measured 10.7% -> 10.9%, and cut. 'Both of my first two occlusion models were made of config constants and both were confidently wrong.'

Real cause: echoCancellation referencing the page's own render stream on speakers + the voice arriving at parity with the bed. AEC off, limiter on speech, PA priority-input lift.

PRIVACY, verified not asserted: mic -> gate -> pa speech bus -> ceiling can -> panners + room convolver -> master -> destination. No MediaRecorder, no ScriptProcessor tap, no buffer outliving a sample, no fetch. Only a smoothed float escapes for the HUD meter. Tracks disabled on key-up and stopped after 20s idle so the tab's recording indicator clears. The dev recordWav() harness CLOSES the mic gate during a take, proven: a 997Hz tone injected past the gate reads +37.6dB over the floor, the same tone arriving through the microphone reads -6dB, i.e. below its own neighbouring noise. Iframe tested cross-origin: without allow=microphone talkStart resolves false in 74ms and never prompts. TALK_LVL journey 0.62 (10dB under the bed - inaudible, joke dead) -> 2.00 (25.7% THD vs the store announcer's 7.0%, past cheap into broken) -> 1.35 (12.9%, +8.3dB over the announcer).

PUSH TO TALK. New src/audio/talk.js + ~50 lines in pa.js/audio.js; API talkStart/talkStop/talkState/talkLevel/talkRelease on createAudio(). Live mic goes straight into the PA speech bus, so it inherits the whole 8-inch ceiling can and the room with no new DSP. PA HOLD-TO-TALK, GAME HALF. [F] is unchanged on a tap - the measured, neutral price-check path is untouched - and the microphone rides on top of it rather than beside it. keydown opens the channel if the handset is free (paReady: desk mode, off cooldown, nothing already held); keyup, blur and a denied permission all close it. talkStart() is a Promise so it is fired and forgotten, and a player who lets go while the browser prompt is still up gets the channel closed on arrival rather than a mic that opens behind him. THE RAMBLE IS WORTH SOMETHING: while you are on the air the subject is standing there listening, so his nine seconds has not started - held.until is pushed forward every frame, capped at HOLD.talkMax 8s so the joke cannot become a strategy. HUD: the PA button goes hot red with a blinking ON AIR pip, a 12-cell level meter off talkLevel(), and a seconds-on-air readout; the meter is the only proof the player has that the store can hear him. Discovery: one ticker line the first time he is at the desk with a working handset ('PA HANDSET LIVE ON THIS TERMINAL - HOLD [F] AND SPEAK'), and the DISPATCH hint reads '[F] HOLD TO TALK' only while the feature is actually available. REFUSAL IS AN ORDINARY ANSWER: denied and unsupported both set talk.denied, the hint reverts to '[F] PA', the discovery line never fires, and he is never asked again for the session. audio.js has not shipped talkStart yet, so today every one of those paths resolves to 'unavailable' and the game is byte-identical to what it was - which is the degraded mode working. PRIVACY: this file never sees a sample. It calls talkStart/talkStop and reads one 0..1 float for the meter; there is deliberately no code path here that could record, store or transmit anything. NO SPEECH RECOGNITION, by design and by instruction.

Step out of his face and no complaint exists. This adds a skill rather than removing a punishment, and it is the one moment where a misread can be unmade - so the eval driver learned the same skill (back off when he turned round and is NOT running; a thief bolts, a shopper complains). Three strikes stays: it is the fiction and the fiction is good.

Root cause was NOT the avoid radius: nav.steer did greedy descent FIRST then filtered, so a corked aisle fouled every point, got=false, and it fell back to 'furthest visible point' — the far side of the cop. The thief sprinted INTO him. Fix prices the cop as a cost inside the Dijkstra flood, but ONLY downstream of the runner: without that filter a cop merely behind prices the ground the thief stands on and the stern chase leaks 1.3% -> 79%.

Confirms the coupling I flagged: observer catch fell 79.4% -> 59.7% once the chase stopped being unlosable, and points fell 1532 -> 912. The old figure was inflated by a chase that auto-caught. The skill separation survives the correction, which is the result that matters.

COUNTERPLAY: the cop is now a COST IN THE ESCAPE FLOOD, not a filter on an already-computed descent. Root cause of the cork: nav.steer's avoid ran AFTER a greedy gradient walk, so it could only pick a nearer point on the same line -- when every point was fouled it fell back to the far side of the cop and the thief sprinted into him. Threat now enters the Dijkstra cost (nav.field opt.avoid), gated to cells downstream of the runner so a pursuer behind him never bends his route. Plus: thief reacts when he SEES the aisle mouth blocked (8.6m, needs LOS + on his route line) instead of walking to 4.5m; tangential (not radial) cop avoidance while running; a committed shoulder-barge whose outcome depends on where the cop was standing when he committed -- hold the lane centre and you have him, drift off one side and he goes past the other for the price of a 0.45s stumble. Per-thief nerve so the route decision is not a pure function of position.
